race_context: The district: Cowan Community School Corporation's boundaries are those of Monroe Township in Delaware County, south of Muncie {wiki_cowan}. The district describes itself as a small rural district serving approximately 800 students at Cowan Elementary (K-6) and Cowan Jr./Sr. High School (7-12) {cw_home}. Christopher Conley is superintendent {cw_h0604}{cw_news}.

The board has five members: Kim Campbell (president, 3 years of service), Rick Jones (vice president, 5 years), Jim Brooks (secretary, 1 year), Paul Hansard (11 years) and Alan Wright (23 years) {cw_board}. The district lists Campbell, Hansard and Wright as up for re-election in 2026 and Jones and Brooks in 2028 {cw_board}. The board meets on the first and third Thursday of each month at 5:30 p.m. {cw_board}.

How members are elected: in 2022 the race appeared as 'Cowan Comm SB At-Large', vote for 3, with Kimberlie Campbell, Paul Hansard and Alan D. Wright as the only candidates {dc_2022}{sp_2022}. In 2024 the Cowan race was vote for 2, with James Allen Brooks Jr. and Charles (Rick) Jones as the two candidates {dc_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the district lists three seats up in 2026 (Campbell, Hansard and Wright), so voters likely may choose up to three, not one as shown on the state list {cw_board}{dc_2022}{in_list}. The election office's 2026 ballot setup was not found to confirm this. Incumbents Wright and Campbell are running again; Hansard is not on the 2026 candidate list, and Tyler Lee Crabtree is the third candidate {in_list}{cw_board}. If three seats are on the ballot, all three candidates would fill them.
Party labels: all three candidates are listed as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Budget (2026): in June 2026 the superintendent reported that the Education Fund ended May in the black, but there were again no transfers from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund {cw_h0624}. On June 4, 2026 the board approved buying 185 Chromebooks and related equipment for $68,820 from the Rainy Day Fund {cw_h0604}. On July 23, 2026 the board approved a resolution to reallocate the Supplemental Homestead Credit and an interlocal agreement with Delaware County for paving {cw_news}. The district posted its proposed 2027 budget (Budget Form 3) and capital projects and bus replacement plans {cw_budget}; budget totals and the effect of the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) were not found in a source read for this profile.

Facilities (2026): in May 2026 the superintendent reported gym roof repairs and an update to elementary electrical switchgear dating from 1975 {cw_h0507}; in July he reported lockers and cabinets installed at the high school, planned window replacements and completed playground drainage work {cw_h0709}{cw_news}.

Enrollment and transfers: in July 2026 the board supported adding a third kindergarten section {cw_h0709}. The district accepts transfer students for 2026-27 and lists 30 approved kindergarten openings {cw_transfer}.

Academics: Cowan High School's 2025 ILEARN proficiency was 38.9% in English/language arts and 28.3% in math, and its 2024 graduation rate was 98.5% with waivers, per the state report card {cw_gps}. The superintendent told the board in May 2026 that spring ILEARN scores would not arrive until September because of new standards {cw_h0507}.

Policies (2026): the board adopted policy updates in June 2026 that the superintendent said include cell phone language needed to comply with the new state law; the district will require phones to be securely stored during the school day {cw_h0604}. A NEOLA artificial-intelligence policy update had a first reading on July 23, 2026 {cw_news}.
Forums: no candidate forum or newspaper questionnaire for this race was found as of Oct. 10, 2026.
